notes: Ed25519 is deterministic (RFC 8032), so every signature here is exact and both implementations must reproduce it byte for byte.
Request and command signatures use standard base64 with padding. Sign-in ticket segments use base64url without padding.
Strings are the exact bytes signed or hashed. In signedString, \n is a single line feed (0x0a); there is no trailing newline.
Cases whose source is account-link are the account link protocol's own published vectors. They are here to show the algorithms are the same ones.
A command case with expect "refused" must fail the signature check when verified as verifyServerId against verifyPublicKey.

A ticket case is redeemed against signInTicketContext at the given now (dashboard clock, unix seconds), from the case's client or, when it has none, from signInTicketContext.client, through steps 3 to 11 of section 9.7. expect is the error code of section 9.7, or ok.

client.whois is tailscaled's WhoIs answer for client.address: an object {login, node}, "not_a_peer" or "unavailable". A loopback address is not asked. deviceCheck is what step 10 records when the ticket is accepted: checked or skipped.
secondRedeem is the result of redeeming the same ticket again, at the same now, from signInTicketContext.client, after the first redeem.

signedString and signature are always exactly what the signer key signed. When altered is absent, payloadSegment is base64url(payloadJson), signedString is signedPrefix + kid + \n + payloadSegment, and ticket is v1.<kid>.<payloadSegment>.<signature>. When altered is set, the ticket was changed after signing as it names (payload_swapped, fifth_part, padded_segment, std_alphabet_signature), payloadSegment is the segment the ticket carries, and those identities need not hold.
payload is null when the JSON text cannot be an object (a repeated key); payloadJson is then the exact text that was encoded.

hubEncoded is true when payloadJson is laid out as Just Hub's encoder writes it: compact, each key once, in the order of the section 9.4 table, next left out when absent. The hub's signer must reproduce ticket byte for byte for every case with expect ok and hubEncoded true.

Amended 2026-11-05 (hub-link-errata.md HL-7 and HL-23): every payload carries tsLogin and tsNode, so every ticket signature changed, and 25 cases were added. Checked by two independent implementations of 9.7 steps 3 to 11 (Go with json.Decoder.Token, and TypeScript).

keys.note: The dashboard's link identity. RFC 8032 test 1; also the account link vectors' server key.
The hub's signing key, pinned at approval. RFC 8032 test 2; also the account link vectors' site key.
A key the dashboard never pinned, used for the wrong-key cases. RFC 8032 test 3.
